fixes.explanation: That's right, friend. Verse 17 says that after the Babylonians defiled her, “…she turned away in disgust.” The Babylonians came to her, and afterward she was the one who turned away from them. Disgust is the word the text uses.

Treasures is a shiny guess, and I'm a cookie stamper, so I respect shiny. But verse 7 says, “She defiled herself with all the idols of those for whom she lusted.” Idols are what the verse names, and no gold gets counted anywhere in it. That's the word to hold onto.

Gifts is a kind guess, friend, like showing up to a party with a plate of cookies. But nothing in verse 16 hands anybody a present. It says, “At the sight of them, she lusted for them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.” What she sends are messengers.

Kings is a big, serious-sounding guess, friend, and I give you credit for aiming high. But verse 27 says, “So I will put an end to your indecency and prostitution, which began in the land of Egypt…” That's the one thing God says He'll end. No crown or throne shows up in that verse.

Taking over land sounds like a reason you'd hear in a big dispute, friend, but this verse isn't one. Verse 31 says, “Because you have followed the path of your sister, I will put her cup into your hand.” The reason is the path she followed. No land changes hands in that sentence.

Never hearing His word is a tempting guess, friend, like blaming a missed text on bad signal. But verse 35 says, “Because you have forgotten Me and have cast Me behind your back, you must bear the consequences of your indecency and prostitution.” The reasons God gives are forgetting Him and casting Him behind her back. Hearing never comes up in that verse.
